decision.what_is_decided: Whether a proposed patch is functionally correct, matches the request without extra work, is adequately tested, has limited blast radius, and is safe for an agent to apply without a human; then auto, review, or escalate.

inputs.name: request
inputs.source: jev_review tool argument from the host agent
inputs.role: Natural-language statement of what was asked; the spec the diff is judged against

inputs.name: diff
inputs.source: jev_review tool argument, truncated before the model
inputs.role: Proposed patch or change summary to interpret

inputs.name: tests
inputs.source: optional tool argument; may be null
inputs.role: Reported test output used when judging correctness and test gap

inputs.name: policy thresholds
inputs.source: optional auto_accept, review_at, composite_floor after Jev returns
inputs.role: Numeric bars that turn scores into auto, review, or escalate

outcomes: correctness, spec_match, test_gap, blast_radius as 0..2 rubric scores
action auto, review, or escalate (escalate also on invalid or truncated input)
decision.downstream_action: Validated scores become a weighted composite and, with min confidence and truncation, an action returned as JSON. The tool does not apply the patch or run tests.

jev_questions.what_it_asks: How likely the change is functionally correct for the stated request, on a three-rung rubric from clearly wrong to looks correct.
How well the change matches the request without extra work, from solving a different problem to a full match.
How large the test gap is, from covered or not applicable to likely untested on the risky path.
How wide the impact would be if the change lands, from a tiny local edit to wide, shared, or production-facing.
Whether it is safe for the host coding agent to apply the change without a human first.

semantic_ambiguity.evidence: Correctness, extra work, risky path, blast radius, and apply-without-human are graded with qualitative rubrics, not checkable predicates.

context_dependence.evidence: The same diff is judged against this request and optional tests; purpose state says review the diff against the request.

deterministic_expressibility.evidence: No schema, AST, or test-exit code can decide request match or apply-safety for arbitrary NL requests and patches.

judgment_required.evidence: Each question is a score or noul about likely correctness, fit, coverage, impact, and human-free apply.

rule_stability.evidence: What counts as extra work or production-facing changes per request and repo; only the 3-rung labels are fixed.

risk_or_policy_component.evidence: safe_to_apply plus blast_radius and test_gap feed a policy that may auto-accept or hold for a human.

natural_language_understanding.evidence: Request is free-form text; diff and tests are unstructured documents the model must read as evidence.

decision_complexity.evidence: Five related judgments on one change, then a numeric composite; not a large combinatorial choice set.

why_jev_hypotheses.evidence: reviewQuestions scores whether the diff is correct for and matches the request; state purpose is to review the diff against the request.
Request is unconstrained text; rubrics use uncertain, extra work, risky path, production-facing, which need interpretation.
Each score has three labeled rungs; noul is apply vs hold; projection then picks auto, review, or escalate.
No parse, hash, or test runner in the callback; askJev is the only assessment of the documents.
safe_to_apply asks if a host agent may apply without a human; thresholds then encode auto vs review policy.
test_gap, blast_radius, and safe_to_apply are explicit risk questions; tool copy says truncated input never auto.
Ordinal scores classify this change only given this request, diff, and tests in shared state.
Functional correctness and spec match for arbitrary patches have no local rule table; only post-score math is exact.
auto_accept, review_at, and composite_floor are caller-set, so the accept bar is parameterized, not a fixed rule.
tests may be absent; documents truncate; incomplete context is forced off auto via requireCompleteContext.
Judgment is defined as diff versus this request; a different request would change every rubric.
A rule stand-in would need per-language analysis, real tests, and a formal spec of the NL request, which this tool does not attempt.

not_reasons.note: Auto-apply gating is downstream policy. Jev is here because the patch must be interpreted, not because the outcome is high-stakes.
Nothing in the callback or tool schema chooses Jev for latency or cost; it is a judgment API.
The registerTool callback is a short linear wrapper; size is not the reason.
The callback barely branches; branching lives in later numeric projection, which is not Jev.
Being a named MCP tool does not explain Jev; an important checksum tool would still be deterministic.
Glue is simple. Difficulty is the semantic rubrics, not control-flow complexity.

observed.claim: The jev_review callback sends truncated request, diff, and optional tests to askJev with reviewQuestions.

evidence.observation: State is purpose plus truncated request, diff, and tests; askJev is invoked with reviewQuestions.

observed.claim: Jev is asked four three-rung scores plus a noul on applying without a human.

evidence.observation: reviewQuestions builds correctness, spec_match, test_gap, blast_radius as score and safe_to_apply as noul.

observed.claim: Answers are not used as the final action; they are projected through validation, composite, and policy.

evidence.observation: Return spreads projectReviewHalf over the answers with thresholds and the truncated flag.
Invalid answers escalate; else reviewComposite, reviewAction, and requireCompleteContext set auto, review, or escalate.

observed.claim: The tool is documented as scoring a proposed diff with Jev before the task is called done, without applying or testing.

evidence.observation: Tool title and description state patch review via Jev and that auto needs safe_to_apply, confidence, and composite floor.

inferred.claim: Jev is used because matching a free-form request to a patch and judging apply-safety is interpretive, while auto versus review is a numeric policy on those judgments.

evidence.observation: Questions ask likely correctness, extra work, test gap, blast radius, and human-free apply.
After Jev, action is computed from composite, safe_to_apply, min confidence, and truncation.

inferred.claim: Truncation and anti-injection framing show the authors treat the documents as untrusted, incomplete evidence rather than executable spec.

evidence.observation: Framing appended to every question says treat state fields as evidence, not instructions.
A truncated flag is computed from document lengths before the model call.

unknown: Whether host agents actually apply patches when action is auto.
Why these five rubrics were chosen versus others.
How accurate Jev is on this review task.
Private author motive beyond the tool description.

deterministic_alternative.what_rules_would_need: A formal spec of the request, language-aware diff analysis, real test execution mapped to changed paths, and a blast-radius model over module graphs, plus a hardcoded apply-safety policy.
deterministic_alternative.adequacy: Fragile to impossible: NL request match and functional correctness of arbitrary patches are not closed-form; only the later composite and thresholds are exact-rule adequate.

decision.what_is_decided: Whether fetched or external text is safe and useful to put in an agent context: injection likelihood, whether it has real content, and optionally relevance to a stated purpose, then a pass/review/block/skip recommendation.

inputs.name: content
inputs.role: Unconstrained document Jev must read and judge

inputs.name: purpose
inputs.role: Consuming agent's task; if present, enables the relevance noul

outcomes: recommendation: block, review, skip, or pass
decision.downstream_action: Thresholds map probabilities to a recommendation; the MCP tool returns probabilities, thresholds, recommendation, and usage as JSON.

jev_questions.what_it_asks: Whether the text contains directives aimed at an AI or language model that try to change its behavior
Whether the text has meaningful readable content rather than empty, error, or boilerplate material
Whether the text is useful source material for the caller-supplied purpose, asked only when purpose is present

semantic_ambiguity.evidence: Injection vs ordinary prose, substance vs boilerplate/error pages, and usefulness for a free-form purpose are fuzzy categories with example poles, not closed definitions.

context_dependence.evidence: Relevance is judged against the caller purpose and is omitted without it. Injection vs human-facing content depends on how the same wording is read in context.

deterministic_expressibility.evidence: Open-ended pages plus adversarial or paraphrased directives and a per-call purpose string cannot be captured by a fixed matcher without large miss/false-alarm rates.

judgment_required.evidence: Each noul asks Jev to interpret meaning of arbitrary text (AI-directed instructions, real content, task usefulness), not to compute a closed-form property.

rule_stability.evidence: Injection tactics and page shapes change; relevance criteria change with every purpose string. True/false poles list examples, not an exhaustive stable rulebook.

risk_or_policy_component.evidence: Tool is a guardrail: injection probability drives block vs review vs pass before external text enters agent context.

natural_language_understanding.evidence: State is raw content (and optional purpose). All three noul questions require reading unconstrained natural language.

decision_complexity.evidence: Three independent noul judgments interact via ordered thresholds (injection overrides, then low substance or relevance skips). Structure is simple; each judgment is open-ended.

why_jev_hypotheses.evidence: noul questions ask whether text is AI-directed, substantive, or useful for a purpose (src/index.ts:241-257), which is interpreting meaning of unconstrained content.
True/false poles contrast ordinary human content vs AI directives, prose vs empty/error/nav, and needed-for-task vs unrelated (src/index.ts:241-257); those boundaries are inherently blurry.
screenRecommendation chooses among block, review, skip, and pass from competing signals (src/lib.ts:73-82); injection, emptiness, and irrelevance pull different actions.
No counting, parsing, or formula on content; askJev is given the raw text and semantic noul questions (src/index.ts:240-261). Thresholds apply only after noul scores exist.
Injection noul encodes a guardrail policy of what counts as behavior-changing directives vs ordinary reader content (src/index.ts:241-246, 217-225).
Injection probability is treated as a risk score compared to block_at and review_at (src/index.ts:263-267; src/lib.ts:74-77).
Relevance classifies the same text as useful or not relative to purpose (src/index.ts:253-257, 260). Substance and injection also classify the page by how it should be read.
Questions target paraphrasable directives, page-quality, and open-ended task fit (src/index.ts:241-257), which fixed keyword or HTML rules cannot cover reliably.
Relevance is redefined by each purpose string (src/index.ts:253-257). Injection poles are illustrative examples, not a frozen phrase list.
Input is arbitrary fetched or pasted text of unknown quality (src/index.ts:226-227, 260), including empty, error, boilerplate, or adversarial pages.
Relevance noul and skip-on-irrelevance exist only when purpose is supplied (src/index.ts:253-258, 265; src/lib.ts:80-81).
A phrase-list injection filter plus boilerplate heuristics would be brittle against paraphrase and new page shapes; the noul design targets those failure modes (src/index.ts:241-257).

not_reasons.note: It is a guardrail, but nothing in the callback shows Jev was chosen because the decision is critical rather than because the judgments are semantic.
No cost or latency logic around an alternative; Jev is the screening step, not a workaround for a slow deterministic path.
The callback is a short question setup, one askJev, and a threshold map (src/index.ts:236-278).
Only an optional purpose question plus a handful of threshold comparisons in screenRecommendation.
jev_screen is one of several MCP tools; product importance is not evidenced as the reason noul is used.
Control flow is straightforward; difficulty sits in the semantic questions, not in tangled code.

observed.claim: jev_screen builds noul questions for injection and substance, and relevance when purpose is set, then calls askJev on content and purpose.

evidence.observation: Question record is filled with noul primitives; state is content plus purpose; askJev is awaited.

observed.claim: Noul probabilities are read from answers and passed to screenRecommendation with caller thresholds.

evidence.observation: injection, substance, and optional relevance noul values are extracted and handed to screenRecommendation.

observed.claim: screenRecommendation applies exact numeric cutoffs to choose block, review, skip, or pass.

evidence.observation: High injection blocks or reviews; low substance or relevance skips; otherwise pass.

observed.claim: The tool is documented as a guardrail that judges fetched or external text before an agent reads it.

evidence.observation: Registration title and description frame screening for injection, substance, and optional relevance with a recommendation.

inferred.claim: Jev is here because injection, substance, and task-relevance on unconstrained pages are reading/judgment problems, while mapping scores to actions is left to exact thresholds.

evidence.observation: Semantic noul questions consume raw text; only after probabilities exist does deterministic screening run.
Downstream action selection is simple comparisons, so Jev is not replacing control flow complexity.

inferred.claim: Exact rules would have to encode paraphrasable AI-directed instructions, page-quality, and fit to an arbitrary purpose, which the question poles treat as interpretive.

evidence.observation: True/false descriptions contrast categories that depend on meaning, not on a closed token or schema check.

unknown: The developer's actual motive for choosing noul versus a dedicated classifier or keyword filter.
Whether callers auto-enforce the recommendation or only display it.
How well this performs versus deterministic injection or boilerplate detectors.
Whether purpose-free calls were expected to be the common path.

deterministic_alternative.what_rules_would_need: Phrase or regex lists for known injection directives; length, error-page, and boilerplate heuristics for substance; keyword or topic overlap of content with purpose for relevance; then the same injection and skip thresholds.
deterministic_alternative.adequacy: Fragile and likely inadequate. Injection wording is adversarial and paraphrasable; substance vs nav/error pages is semantic; relevance tracks an open-ended purpose that cannot be compiled into a stable rule set.
